mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) at or below 0.1% compresses equity discount rates and signals accommodative monetary policy, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as market participants price in lower financing costs.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS <= 0.1%, with a t-test p-value > 0.05 for the mean return being positive.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month unemployment rate (UNRATE) increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS <= 0.1%) and high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 235) indicate a 'growth vs. inflation' trade-off where markets anticipate future tightening, generating negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05 in a regression with interaction term).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1000 thousand units, it signals robust residential construction and consumer confidence, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as economic expansion accelerates.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST > 1000, or the average return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month industrial production (INDPRO) decline below 100 indicates manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate output and earnings visibility, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as the market prices in economic slowdown.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100, or the average return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS) exceeding 100,000 new jobs per month compresses unemployment and boosts consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as earnings growth accelerates.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS growth > 100,000, or the average return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a high-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 235), the Federal Reserve is expected to tighten policy, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as discount rates rise and growth expectations decline.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 235, or the average return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent high housing starts (HOUST > 1000) and strong retail sales (RSAFS > 440,000 million dollars) indicate robust consumer demand that accelerates corporate earnings, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05 in a regression with interaction term).
